'''Nar Hida''' was a [[Luptoomian]]<ref name="BMF50" /> [[human]]<ref name="SWTVE" /> who left the [[planet]] [[Coruscant]] as a [[freighter tramper]] on board the [[AA-9 Freighter-Liner]] ''[[Jendirian Valley]]''<ref name="BMF50" /> in [[22 BBY]].<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of {{Film|II}} to [[22 BBY]].</ref> The [[freighter]] took off from [[Westport]] on Coruscant headed for the [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid Rim]] [[planet]] [[Naboo]].<ref name="BMF50" /> During the journey, Hida traveled in the cargo hold where<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref> he<ref name="BMF50" /> sat by one of the [[starship]]'s walls as<ref name="AOTC" /> [[flatcake]]s<ref name="AND">[[A New Dawn (novel)|''A New Dawn'']]</ref> were being served to passengers.<ref name="AOTC" /> He wore a spiked [[Color|green]] [[Cape|cloak]]<ref name="SWTVE" /> and was recognizable by his Luptoomian fashion, which made him more noticeable than other passengers like the [[Jedi]] [[Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]], who were both disguised as peasants.<ref name="BMF50" /> He had light skin and blue [[eye]]s.<ref name="SWTVE" />

==Behind the scenes==
Nar Hida appeared in the [[2002]] [[prequel trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']].<ref name="AOTC" /> The scene was filmed in the art department depot of building 48 at [[Fox Studios, Sydney]].<ref name="365Days">''[[Creating the Worlds of Star Wars: 365 Days]]''</ref> In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], the character was identified in "AA-9 Coruscant Starfreighter," an article published in the "[[Starship Fact File]]" department of the magazine [[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon 50|''Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon'' 50]],<ref name="BMF50" /> which was written by [[Tim Veekhoven]]<ref name="Veekhoven">{{DMCite|dm=File:TimVeekhoven-Credits.png|creator=Tim Veekhoven}}</ref> and published around [[December 16]], [[2015]].<ref name="BMFdate">{{BMFdates|50}}</ref>

The name originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where the [[Nar Hida/Legends|character]] was first identified by [[Gregory Walker]],<ref name="Walker">{{Blog|narbflick|9|Nar Hida: The Story Behind the Story}}</ref> under the username "NarbFlick," through the [[StarWars.com]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] feature "[[What's The Story?]]"<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|narhida|Hida, Nar}}</ref> in an entry published on [[September 28]], [[2006]].<ref name="DBDate">{{SWArchive|url=databank/updates/news20060928.html|text=What's the Story, Round 7}}</ref>
